periods.public: The panel discusses the necessity of verifying financial, operational, and staffing constraints. They agree to divide the available data sources to ensure a comprehensive overview of the hospital's current capacity.

lines.Midori: Suggests looking into why previous programs failed.
lines.Jonathan: Proposes checking the actual impact of past trials on patients.
lines.Misaki: Mentions the importance of current staffing levels.
lines.Shion: Questions the long-term financial viability of the budget.
lines.Shizue: Raises concerns about physical infrastructure and booking capacity.

lines.Midori: Agrees to check board minutes and nursing rounds.
lines.Jonathan: Decides to look at readmission figures and booking records.
lines.Misaki: Chooses ward vacancies and the therapy/midwifery review.
lines.Shion: Selects the ledger and regional fund tariffs.
lines.Shizue: Opts for rooms/parking and the booking system.

periods.public: Participants share their findings regarding budget cuts, staffing gaps, and infrastructure bottlenecks. They debate the risks of off-site work versus the lack of available on-site space.

lines.Midori: Reports on the failure of joint-department clinics.
lines.Jonathan: Shares that previous call-back trials reduced readmissions.
lines.Misaki: Notes the shortage of ward nurses but slack in midwifery.
lines.Shion: Points out the budget decrease and tariff issues for off-site work.
lines.Shizue: Highlights the lack of parking and room availability.

lines.Midori: Warns about the difficulty of shared nursing rounds.
lines.Jonathan: Mentions that unbooked work disappears from reports.
lines.Misaki: Asks how staffing slack can be utilized.
lines.Shion: Argues that on-site programs are more financially sustainable.
lines.Shizue: Questions how any new program fits into the full booking system.

lines.Midori: Suggests avoiding programs that rely on outside bodies.
lines.Jonathan: Discusses the value of evidence-based patient outcomes.
lines.Misaki: Points out the risk of adding pressure to ward nurses.
lines.Shion: Emphasizes the need for a program that generates revenue.
lines.Shizue: Notes the limited shuttle coverage for remote villages.

periods.public: The panel evaluates the candidates against the discovered constraints. They weigh the benefits of patient outcomes against staffing availability and financial risk before voting.

lines.Midori: Evaluates the candidates based on departmental cooperation.
lines.Jonathan: Compares the candidates based on patient impact data.
lines.Misaki: Analyzes which candidate fits the current staffing slack.
lines.Shion: Assesses the candidates based on the ledger and tariffs.
lines.Shizue: Checks which candidate requires the least amount of new space.

lines.Midori: Discusses the viability of a joint midwifery-pediatric effort.
lines.Jonathan: Argues for the merits of home follow-up based on trial data.
lines.Misaki: Points out that midwifery has the capacity for new tasks.
lines.Shion: Suggests a dedicated unit to maximize on-site billing.
lines.Shizue: Questions the logistics of home visits versus on-site classes.

lines.Midori: Considers the stability of the proposed staffing models.
lines.Jonathan: Discusses the recording of activity in the booking system.
lines.Misaki: Argues against programs that burden ward nursing.
lines.Shion: Questions the long-term funding of off-site visits.
lines.Shizue: Considers the impact on the car park and shuttle.

lines.Midori: Finalizes her choice based on staffing harmony.
lines.Jonathan: Finalizes his choice based on patient readmission data.
lines.Misaki: Finalizes her choice based on the staffing review.
lines.Shion: Finalizes his choice based on financial logic.
lines.Shizue: Finalizes her choice based on infrastructure capacity.

seats.Shion: Focuses on the long-term financial sustainability and revenue. He uses logical arguments to highlight budget deficits and tariff losses.
seats.Midori: Concerned with the stability of inter-departmental agreements. She looks for programs that avoid the pitfalls of previous failed collaborations.
seats.Jonathan: Values empirical evidence of patient benefit. He analyzes past trial data to determine which approach actually improves health outcomes.
seats.Shizue: Worries about the physical and systemic capacity of the hospital. She evaluates proposals based on their impact on parking, rooms, and scheduling.
seats.Misaki: Focuses on the distribution of labor and staff burnout. She seeks a program that aligns with existing staffing surpluses rather than deficits.
